newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne again rejects Invacare's latest bid.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne again rejects Invacare's latest bid.

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc. said Thursday that its board rejected Invacare Corp.'s increased tender offer of $13.50 a share, or $167.4 million, as a three-month standoff between the two providers of home healthcare products became more acrimonious.

In announcing its rejection of Invacare's latest unsolicited offer, Healthdyne accused its rival of making "false, insulting, and self-serving" insinuations about the financial performance of Healthdyne.

Healthdyne, which is based in Marietta, Ga., previously rejected Invacare offers of $12.50 and $13 a share. It said its board believed the latest offer was "still grossly inadequate" and reconfirmed its determination that a sale was not in the best interests of the company or its shareholders.

The company also released a letter it sent to Invacare Chairman A. Malachi Mixon accusing him of making "misleading and self-serving comments" in his attempt "to buy Healthdyne Technologies at a bargain price."

The latter, signed by Healthdyne Chairman Parker H. Petit, said the company expected to meet or exceed analysts' forecasts for its first-quarter financial results and expected its stock to be valued in excess of the latest offer.
The company said it expected first-quarter results to be "excellent," driven by strong revenue growth from its new products.
According to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates, the consensus for Healthdyne's first quarter was 13 cents a share, compared with 14 cents in the previous first quarter.
Healthdyne's stock was trading at $14 a share, unchanged from Wednesday, in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
The letter, which labeled Invacare a "low tech" company, said Healthdyne was prepared to engage in a proxy battle with Invacare at its upcoming annual meeting, which has not yet been scheduled.
The letter indicated that Healthdyne was waiting until it reported its first-quarter results before scheduling the shareholders meeting.
"We simply will not allow you to dictate the timetable to suit your own objective, which is to buy Healthdyne Technologies at a bargain price," the letter said.
"Although we had hoped to avoid the expense of a proxy contest, that now appears unavoidable," it added.

Healthdyne again recommended that its stockholders reject Invacare's latest tender offer. On March 25 Healthdyne said that only 18 percent of its outstanding shares were tendered in response to Invacare's $13 offer.
Shares of Invacare, which is based in Elyria, Ohio, lost 25 cents to $21.75 on the Nasdaq market.
Both companies make medical products that are used in the home or in clinical settings.
